summary: SET owns the shape of Calendaric's configuration (what is stored per granularity versus what is global), the settings screen that edits it, persisting it safely across restarts and hand-edits, and the guarantee that a saved change reaches the rest of the plugin without restarting Obsidian. It stops at the boundary of what a value means: FMT decides whether a format string is valid, TPL decides what a template does, NOTE decides how a folder is used to create a note, and MIG owns importing configuration from other plugins and upgrading old stored shapes — SET owns the field that holds each of those values and the feedback shown when a value is rejected.

stories.title: Per-granularity configuration model
stories.story: As someone managing several kinds of periodic notes, I want every granularity's own settings kept separate from every other granularity's, so that changing one period's folder or format never disturbs another period's configuration.
stories.rationale: Per-granularity isolation is what lets day, week, month and year notes live in different folders with different formats and templates without interfering with each other.

acceptance_criteria.given: the plugin's stored configuration
then: it has its own enabled flag, filename format, folder, template path and allow-prefix-matching value
none of these values are shared with, or derived from, another granularity's settings
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/settings/model.test.ts > AC-SET-01.1 every granularity owns its own five values.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user changes the allow-prefix-matching toggle for one granularity

every other granularity's stored settings remain unchanged
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/settings/model.test.ts > AC-SET-01.2 an allow-prefix-matching change touches one granularity only.

acceptance_criteria.given: the stored configuration contains an additional named configuration group beyond the single one currently in use
acceptance_criteria.when: the plugin loads the configuration and then saves it again unchanged
then: the extra group's data is preserved exactly
the in-use group's data is preserved exactly
no control for creating, renaming or switching between groups is shown to the user
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/settings/model.test.ts > AC-SET-01.3 an extra named group survives a load and save, for the two preservation clauses. The third clause (no create/rename/switch control is shown) is settled by code review: settings.ts has no configuration-group control at all -- every "group" identifier there names a per-granularity visual section (periodic-group), not a configuration set.

acceptance_criteria.when: the user disables it on the settings screen
then: its format, folder, template and allow-prefix-matching values remain stored unchanged
re-enabling the granularity later shows those same values rather than blanks or defaults
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/settings/model.test.ts > AC-SET-01.4 disabling a granularity keeps its configured values.

acceptance_criteria.given: a fresh install with no configuration ever saved
acceptance_criteria.when: the plugin loads for the first time
then: exactly one implicit configuration group exists
the user is not asked to name, choose or create a group
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/settings/model.test.ts > AC-SET-01.5 a fresh install has exactly one implicit group, on loadStoredConfig(undefined); this now describes real plugin behaviour because main.ts:105-113 routes loadSettings/saveSettings through loadStoredConfig/toSettings/applySettings. The second clause (the user is not asked to name, choose or create a group) is settled by code review as an absence: no such prompt or control exists in settings.ts or the modal. The criterion is testable_by integration and no run against a live Obsidian host was performed.

stories.title: Global settings live alongside per-granularity settings
stories.story: As someone configuring Calendaric, I want settings that apply to the whole plugin kept separate from any single granularity's settings, so that I can find and change a plugin-wide option without opening every granularity's section.
stories.rationale: Global and per-granularity settings answer different questions, and mixing them makes the screen for either harder to read.

acceptance_criteria.given: the settings screen
then: global settings appear in an area that is visually and structurally separate from any granularity's own settings

acceptance_criteria.given: a global setting is changed
then: it is stored exactly once in the configuration, not once per granularity

acceptance_criteria.given: a fresh install whose global settings were never opened or changed
acceptance_criteria.when: the settings screen is opened for the first time
then: every global setting shows its documented built-in default value
no global setting appears blank or undefined

acceptance_criteria.given: the settings screen
then: a control for the word-count threshold that decides how many dots a day shows is visible among the global settings
on a fresh install, that control shows a default value of 250

acceptance_criteria.given: the user enters a value into the word-count threshold field that is not a positive whole number, for example zero, a negative number, or text
then: the stored word-count threshold falls back to the default of 250
the settings field shows a message explaining that the value fell back to the default

decisions.title: Words per dot is a global setting with a default of 250
decisions.decision: Calendaric keeps the word-count threshold that decides how many dots a day shows. It is one global number, default 250, editable in settings. A value that is not a positive whole number falls back to the default and the settings field says so. The Calendar import carries the existing wordsPerDot value across.
decisions.rationale: US-CAL-07 requires configured word-count thresholds while SET named no control and no default, and MIG dropped the existing value on the claim that Calendaric has no equivalent field. An implementation could satisfy every criterion and still leave the user no way to configure the behaviour CAL promises. This vault's Calendar plugin has wordsPerDot 250, so the default matches what the user already sees.

stories.title: Resolve effective settings for a granularity from a single source of truth
stories.story: As someone relying on periodic notes, I want each granularity's effective format, folder and template to resolve to one predictable value, so that I never have to guess which of several possible sources of that setting actually won.
stories.rationale: The old plugins let format, folder and template be set in more than one place at once; a single resolver removes the guesswork the vault currently gets right only by coincidence.

acceptance_criteria.given: a granularity's format field is left empty
then: a documented built-in default format for that granularity is used
no error is raised and no undefined value is returned
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/settings/model.test.ts > "AC-SET-03.1: uses the documented built-in default format when a granularity's format is empty" and "AC-SET-03.1: returns a defined value for every field of every granularity". DEFAULT_FORMATS in src/settings/model.ts is now the single table; it replaced the settings-screen placeholder and the import's DEFAULT_DAY_FORMAT, which were two more copies. Mutation-checked by the orchestrator: deleting the empty-format substitution fails 2 of the 41 tests.

acceptance_criteria.given: a granularity's folder and template path fields are both left empty
then: the folder resolves to the vault root
no template is applied
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/settings/model.test.ts > "AC-SET-03.2: resolves an unset folder to the vault root and applies no template". The resolver returns "" for an unset folder, which src/notes/noteUtils.ts:86 already treats as the vault root. The "default new-file location" fallback at noteUtils.ts:73 is deliberately untouched: it belongs to AC-NOTE-03.2, which is already pass, and moving it here would reopen a closed criterion.

acceptance_criteria.given: the same granularity's settings are needed by two different parts of the plugin at the same moment, for example note creation and the calendar view
then: both receive identical format, folder, template and allow-prefix-matching values
acceptance_criteria.evidence: HALF SETTLED, and the missing half is wiring, not correctness. vitest: src/settings/model.test.ts > "AC-SET-03.3: hands two callers the same format, folder, template and prefix-match values" and "AC-SET-03.3: is unaffected by a caller that writes to the config it was handed" prove the resolver is deterministic and returns a fresh object per call; mutation-checked by the orchestrator (returning the stored object itself fails 3 tests). But no consumer calls it yet: src/ui/calendar.ts and src/notes/noteCreate.ts still read settings[granularity] directly, so two parts of the running plugin can still disagree. The criterion is about two callers agreeing, so it stays unverified until the consumers are wired. Deliberately not done in this ticket: US-NOTE-04 and US-CAL-02 own those two files right now and the edit would collide.

acceptance_criteria.given: the same logical daily-note setting exists both in Calendaric's own stored configuration and in an unrelated external file that disagrees with it, as recorded for this vault
acceptance_criteria.when: Calendaric resolves the effective daily-note settings
then: Calendaric's own stored configuration is used

acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/settings/model.test.ts:542 > "AC-SET-03.4: resolves the daily note from Calendaric's own configuration, never the external Daily Notes file". The test first proves the external file is present, readable and disagreeing on all three fields, by running decideDailyNotesCard against a read-counting port; it then resolves and asserts the read counter did not move. An assertion on the resolved values alone would pass even if the file were read.

stories.title: Format, folder and template fields show validity feedback
stories.story: As someone typing a filename format, folder or template path into settings, I want to see immediately whether it is valid, so that I catch a mistake before it silently affects note creation.
stories.rationale: A field that only fails much later, when a note is actually created, wastes the time between making the mistake and discovering it.

acceptance_criteria.given: the user types a value into a granularity's format field
then: an inline message next to the field explains what is wrong

acceptance_criteria.given: the user types a value into a granularity's folder field that does not match an existing location in the vault

the value is still saved to the stored configuration
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest src/settings.fieldValidity.test.ts 'AC-SET-04.2: a folder that does not exist warns on blur and is still saved' plus two more 04.2 tests; red when the blur check, the not-yet-created warning, or the folder save is removed (orchestrator mutations)

acceptance_criteria.given: the user types a value into a granularity's template field that does not resolve to an existing file

acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest src/settings.fieldValidity.test.ts 'AC-SET-04.3: a missing template errors on blur and is still saved'; red when the blur check is removed (orchestrator mutation)

acceptance_criteria.given: any of the format, folder or template fields currently shows a warning for a value that was saved (an error-level format is never saved, per AC-FMT-05.1, so reopening shows the last saved format instead)
acceptance_criteria.when: the settings screen is closed and reopened

acceptance_criteria.given: the user wants help constructing a format string

The guide now opens as https://github.com/matisnape/obsidian-calendaric/blob/master/docs/guide.md because an installed plugin folder has no docs/guide.md (orchestrator decision)

acceptance_criteria.given: the plugin's manifest.json
then: isDesktopOnly is declared true
no criterion in this settings area promises the plugin installs or runs on a mobile Obsidian client

decisions.title: Desktop first, with every desktop-only API behind one boundary
decisions.decision: manifest.json declares isDesktopOnly: true. Any call into a desktop-only API lives behind a single adapter, so supporting mobile later means replacing that adapter rather than reworking the views.
decisions.rationale: The repository currently declares isDesktopOnly: false while calling an Electron API, which is a lie that fails at runtime on mobile. Declaring the truth costs nothing now; isolating the call keeps the option open.

decisions.title: The first release is desktop only, and says so in the manifest
decisions.decision: manifest.json declares isDesktopOnly true, which means Obsidian will not install Calendaric on a phone or tablet. No story may promise phone behaviour while that stands. Hover-dependent surfaces still need a pointer-free path, because a desktop user can be on a keyboard or a touchscreen laptop, but that is an accessibility requirement, not a mobile one. Mobile support is an icebox entry, gated on replacing the desktop-only call behind DEC-03's adapter.
decisions.rationale: DEC-03 already declared desktop only, and US-CAL-08 was written for a laptop and a phone. Both cannot hold: isDesktopOnly true blocks installation on mobile outright, so a phone criterion could never be run, let alone passed. Desktop first without closing the door is the stated position, and one adapter plus an icebox entry is what keeps the door open.

stories.title: Only one granularity can open automatically at startup
stories.story: As someone who wants exactly one note to greet them when Obsidian opens, I want turning on 'Open on startup' for one granularity to turn it off for every other granularity, so that I never end up with two notes racing to open at once.
stories.rationale: Two granularities both trying to auto-open at startup is a contradiction the settings screen has to resolve for the user, not leave as an ambiguous stored state.

acceptance_criteria.given: granularity A currently has 'Open on startup' switched on
acceptance_criteria.when: the user switches 'Open on startup' on for granularity B
then: granularity A's toggle switches off automatically
the settings screen shows A as off immediately, without the user reopening or reloading it
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest src/settings.startupExclusive.test.ts 'AC-SET-05.1: switching B on switches A off and the redrawn screen shows A off' drives the real toggles and reads the redrawn screen; red when clearStartupNote is removed from settings.ts and red when the display() redraw is removed (orchestrator mutations)

acceptance_criteria.given: no granularity currently has 'Open on startup' switched on
acceptance_criteria.when: the user switches it on for one granularity
then: that granularity is the only one left with the flag on
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest src/settings.startupExclusive.test.ts 'AC-SET-05.2: switching one on with none on leaves only that one on'

acceptance_criteria.given: a granularity's 'Open on startup' is currently on
acceptance_criteria.when: the user switches it off directly
then: no other granularity's 'Open on startup' value changes
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest src/settings.startupExclusive.test.ts 'AC-SET-05.3: switching one off changes no other granularity'

acceptance_criteria.given: the stored configuration has more than one granularity marked 'Open on startup' at once, for example after the file was edited by hand
then: it shows the stored state honestly, without silently picking one for the user
the next time the user switches any granularity's flag on, only that one remains on afterward
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest src/settings.startupExclusive.test.ts 'AC-SET-05.4: a stored config with two flags on loads and displays both, rewriting nothing' (through plugin.loadSettings; red when loadSettings clears a flag, orchestrator mutation) and 'AC-SET-05.4: from two flags on, the next switch-on leaves only that one on'

stories.title: Persist settings and recover from partial or invalid stored data
stories.story: As someone whose settings file can be edited outside the plugin, I want Calendaric to keep working even when the stored configuration is incomplete or malformed, so that one bad or missing field never breaks the whole plugin.
stories.rationale: The configuration file is plain text the user or another tool can touch directly, so the plugin cannot assume it is always well-formed.

acceptance_criteria.given: a change is made anywhere on the settings screen
acceptance_criteria.when: the change is committed, for example a field loses focus or a toggle is switched
then: the change is written to the plugin's persisted configuration immediately
no separate 'Save' action is required
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/settings/persistence.test.ts: "AC-SET-06.1: every committed change on the settings screen writes the configuration" and "AC-SET-06.1: one committed field change reaches the disk on its own". The first walks every commit handler in src/settings.ts and requires each to call this.save(); the second drives the real plugin's saveSettings() over a stand-in loadData/saveData and watches the write land. Mutations: deleting `await this.save();` from the allow-prefix-matching handler in src/settings.ts took 18 passed to 1 failed | 17 passed; deleting `await this.saveData(next);` from saveSettings in src/main.ts took 18 passed to 4 failed | 14 passed. Both restored to 18 passed.

acceptance_criteria.given: Obsidian is closed and reopened
then: every setting the user previously saved is restored exactly as it was left
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/settings/persistence.test.ts: "AC-SET-06.2: restores every stored setting when the plugin loads again" and "AC-SET-06.2: survives a second close and reopen without drifting". Every editable key is moved off its default, saved through the real plugin, read back by a second plugin over the same JSON, and compared whole. Mutation: applySettings writing `...pickGlobals(stored)` instead of `...pickGlobals(settings)` in src/settings/model.ts took 18 passed to 2 failed | 16 passed, restored 18 passed.

acceptance_criteria.given: the persisted configuration file is missing a field entirely, for example because it was hand-edited
then: the missing field is filled with its built-in default
the plugin finishes loading normally
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/settings/persistence.test.ts: "AC-SET-06.3: fills every missing field of a half-written granularity", plus the three sibling AC-SET-06.3 cases for the globals, for every granularity being complete after the load, and for no stored configuration at all. Mutation: `format: asString(raw.format, DEFAULT_PERIODIC_CONFIG.format)` changed to `format: raw.format as string` in normalizeConfig (src/settings/model.ts) took 18 passed to 2 failed | 16 passed — both failures inside AC-SET-06.3 — restored 18 passed.

acceptance_criteria.given: the persisted configuration contains a field with an unexpected type or shape
then: that field falls back to its default
every other, well-formed field in the same configuration loads unaffected
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/settings/persistence.test.ts: "AC-SET-06.4: writes a malformed granularity back as a configuration, not as its characters", with "AC-SET-06.4: replaces a granularity of the wrong shape, leaving the others as stored" and "AC-SET-06.4: replaces a global of the wrong type with its default, one field at a time" covering the load side. The load side already held before this story; the save side did not, and the guard added to applySettings is what this criterion bought. Mutation: dropping that guard (`isRecord(storedConfig) ? { ...storedConfig } : {}` back to `{ ...storedConfig }` in src/settings/model.ts) took 18 passed to 1 failed | 17 passed, restored 18 passed — the stored `day: "garbage"` came back out as {"0":"g","1":"a",...}.

acceptance_criteria.given: the complete set of keys the plugin persists and shows as editable
acceptance_criteria.when: each key is checked against the plugin's own runtime code
then: every persisted, user-editable key has at least one place in the plugin that reads it
no setting is stored and shown as editable while nothing in the plugin ever uses its value
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/settings/persistence.test.ts: "AC-SET-06.5: every persisted, user-editable key has at least one production reader", held in place by "AC-SET-06.5: finds the keys the settings screen makes editable" and "AC-SET-06.5: every key the screen edits is one the plugin persists". The audit reads the ten editable keys off src/settings.ts and looks for a read of each outside the writer, the storage model and the type declarations; all ten have one, so no setting is stored and shown as editable while nothing uses it. Mutation: removing the only production read of openAtStartup (`if (!config.openAtStartup || !config.enabled) continue;` to `if (!config.enabled) continue;` in src/main.ts) took 18 passed to 1 failed | 17 passed with `expected [ 'openAtStartup' ] to deeply equal []`, restored 18 passed.

shared_coverage.cal:persist-plugin-settings: Persisting settings is the same write for both stories: US-SET-06 specifies what survives a reload, US-SET-07 that a saved value takes effect at once.

stories.title: A saved setting takes effect immediately
stories.story: As someone tuning periodic-note settings while Obsidian is open, I want the rest of the plugin to pick up my change the instant it is saved, so that I never have to restart Obsidian to see the effect.
stories.rationale: A setting that only applies after a restart makes every change feel risky to try.

acceptance_criteria.given: the calendar view is open and a granularity's folder or format is changed on the settings screen
then: the calendar redraws to reflect the change without the view being reopened or Obsidian being restarted

acceptance_criteria.given: a granularity's folder is changed on the settings screen
acceptance_criteria.when: that granularity's note is next looked up or created
then: the newly saved folder is used, not the folder that was in effect when Obsidian started

acceptance_criteria.given: a granularity is switched from disabled to enabled, or the reverse, on the settings screen
then: the commands for that granularity appear or disappear immediately, without restarting Obsidian

acceptance_criteria.given: a settings change fails to persist, for example because the write to disk fails
then: the rest of the plugin keeps operating on the last successfully saved configuration
no part of the plugin ends up running on a half-applied change

shared_coverage.cal:persist-plugin-settings: Persisting settings is the same write for both stories: US-SET-06 specifies what survives a reload, US-SET-07 that a saved value takes effect at once.

uncovered.reason: This is the breadcrumb router that moved the settings screen between a calendar-set list page and a calendar-set detail page. With calendar sets in the icebox and exactly one implicit configuration group (US-SET-01), the settings screen has one page and nothing to navigate between; the router's own behaviour (for example that it always resets to the dashboard on close) has no equivalent to carry forward.

notes: Of the 80 mapped settings-map rows, most are the SAME logical field recorded once per source plugin (dni, cal, pn, calendaric, vault, forks); they do not each need a distinct key in the new model. Concluded canonical survivors: 6 per-granularity fields (enabled, format, folder, templatePath, openAtStartup, allowPrefixMatch) for day/week/month/year, plus roughly 7 global fields (week start, show week numbers, confirm-before-create, locale override, words-per-dot, the single implicit configuration group, and the internal daily-notes-import-shown flag).

Dropped as explicitly dead (stored and editable but never read by anything, per the map's own notes): cal's weeklyNoteFormat/weeklyNoteTemplate/weeklyNoteFolder, pn's hasMigratedDailyNoteSettings, hasMigratedWeeklyNoteSettings, installedVersion, and pn's dead-duplicate ISettings localeOverride/weekStart fields. AC-SET-06.5 asserts none of these come back.

Dropped as icebox-scoped, not because they are wrong: every quarterly-granularity row (periodic-notes.settings.quarterly.*, the vault's calendarSets[].quarter, and the placeholder Monthly/Quarterly/Yearly UI groups), enableTimelineComplication, and calendar-set plurality (activeCalendarSet as a user-facing choice). The underlying array/id may still exist internally as the single implicit group's id; it is just never exposed as a choice.

Collapsed as duplicate multi-source read paths now replaced by one source of truth (US-SET-03): daily-notes.format/folder/template (core plugin copy), calendar.options.weeklyNoteFormat/Folder/Template (legacy Calendar-plugin copy), and every periodic-notes.settings.<granularity>.enabled 'use Periodic Notes settings' precedence flag — with a single stored value per field there is nothing left to choose between.

Out of SET's scope entirely: app.vault.getConfig('weekStart') and ('localeOverride') read Obsidian's own vault-wide config rather than a Calendaric-owned key, and Templater's templates_folder/trigger_on_file_creation_mode/folder_templates and the core daily-notes.json format belong to the plugins MIG imports from, not to Calendaric's own configuration shape.

Roughly a third of the acceptance criteria in this epic are testable_by manual or integration rather than unit, because the behaviour under test is either a live settings-screen interaction (inline validation feedback, the guide link) or requires the calendar view and command palette to observe reactivity end to end.

US-SET-04 and US-SET-06 reference 'invalid stored data' and 'the format/folder/template check fails' without asserting what specifically makes a value invalid — that judgment belongs to FMT (format), NOTE (folder) and TPL (template); this epic only owns that the field shows the feedback and that saving still succeeds.
